title: Comrade Kalyan
plot_overview: In a village on the Andhra-Odisha border, a theatre owner draws on communist sentiment to keep his aging cinema running. He becomes involved with the local naxals and kidnaps a leader, setting a chain of events in motion.
will_you_like_this: You may enjoy this if you’re drawn to stories about rural communities, political movements, and the struggle to keep a local cinema alive; Not for you if you prefer lighter stories without political conflict.
review_summary: Pros: distinctive rural setting; cinema-centered premise | Cons: limited review information; story details are sparse
